# dsh-devlead

A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin suite that
upgrades **one ordinary session** into a **DevLead sessio

n**: it can operate DSH **Workspaces**
and **Sessions** directly, create and continue other Sessions

, read their state, and be woken
when their state changes — so one agent can orchestrate multiple re

positories inside a standard
interface that the human can see and interact with.
**English** · 简体中文

- **A DevLead session = an ordinary session + one durable switch.** Once enabled, that session
gains

8 `devlead_*` tools, a DevLead system prompt, and a status strip above the composer.
The switch its

elf is a **human-only action**; no tool can enable it. While the mode is off,
the UI only shows a sm

all composer-toolbar icon — no permanent bar on every conversation.
- **Dispatcher by default, not i

mplementer.** The DevLead session decides which Workspace owns
each request (from registered Workspa

ce metadata, not by reading another repository's code),
dispatches a self-contained brief to a Sessi

on there, watches it, reviews the delivery, and
reports. Read-only inspection is allowed for writing

the brief and reviewing a delivery; deeper
investigation belongs to the dispatched Session. **Write

s** (file edits, builds, commits,
pushes, deploys) belong to a Session in the owning Workspace — eve

n when the target is the
lead's own workspace — unless the human explicitly authorizes the lead to d

o it directly in
this conversation; direct upkeep of the lead's own record files may follow that rep

ository's
instructions. Subagents and Agent Teams are not a substitute for dispatching the work to a

n
openable ordinary Session.
- **Outputs must be standard DSH entities.** Workspaces are genuinely r

egistered through
[该节后续省略]
## Features
| Capability | Description |
| DevLead mode | One durable switch per session; enabling it adds the `devlead_*` tools, the DevLead

system prompt, and the status strip |
| Role model | Dispatch-first: determine the owning Workspace
from registered metadata, send a self-contained brief to a Session there, watch it, review the deli
very, report; read-only inspection is bounded to the brief and the review, writes stay in the owning
Workspace's Session (including the lead's own workspace; direct work only when the human explicitly
authorizes it in this conversation; record-file upkeep may follow the lead's repository instruction

s) |
| Standard DSH entities | Child sessions are ordinary Sessions (visible in the sidebar; humans

can open and take them over); Workspaces go through `workspaceRegistry`, not subagents |
| Optional
worktree isolation | When the Host composes DSH's experimental Git worktree service (`ctx.worktrees`
), `devlead_create_session` can request `isolation: "worktree"` so a writing Session gets its own br
anch and checkout instead of sharing the Workspace checkout; detection is optional and a missing cap
ability degrades to the shared checkout with a reported status, never an error (see Optional worktre

e isolation) |
| 8 model tools | Register/list Workspaces, create/read/continue/watch Sessions, read

the notification digest (see Model tools) |
| Human commands | `/devlead` (status), `/devlead on\|o
ff`, `/devlead reset` (damaged-state recovery), `/devlead watch\|unwatch <session>`; sessions are ad

dressable by full id or unique prefix |
| Notification loop | A watched session's `turn/end` writes
a durable notification and wakes an indexed DevLead through a coalescing window (configurable window
; cold leads are resumed by default); the watch index is rebuilt from durable records after a Host r

estart, and a disposed lead keeps observing (see Notification loop) |
[该节后续省略]
### Requirements
| Item | Requirement |

| DSH | `0.2.2-rc.1` (plugin / bundle packages declare `engines.dsh: >=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.3.0`) |
| Node.

js | ≥ 24.9 (local build / publish only; installing from npm needs no local Node) |
| pnpm | 12.x (C

I pins `pnpm@12.16.1`) |
| Web UI | the DSH desktop app or `dsh web`; DevLead UI renders on the Web

platform only |
| Local E2E | an installed DSH desktop runtime (`dsh` on PATH, or `DSH_BIN`); `pnpm
e2e` boots an isolated instance with it |
## Known limitations

- **One durable mode per Session:** once enabled it stays enabled across DSH restarts and session
re

sumes; a human must run `/devlead off`.
- **Cold leads are resumed by default:** after a Host restar

t / plugin reload the watch index is
rebuilt from durable records, and a queued notification resumes

the cold lead Session unless
`wakeColdSession` is explicitly set to `false` (then the queues wait i

n memory for a human to
open the lead). Resume requires the Host to compose a Session activator; wit

hout it the records
stay durable and are delivered when the Session is opened.
- **The watch index i

s process-local transport:** a disposed lead keeps observing and keeps
recording notifications, and

the index is rebuilt after a restart/reload; only while the plugin
itself is unloaded are settled tu

rns unobserved (the events are not replayed per watcher), so a
turn that ends during an unload is no

t notified.
- **64 retained notifications:** the projection truncates at that constant; older record

s remain
in the Session log.
- **Default caps of 64 watched / 200 listed:** configurable; the comman

d's candidate list is
capped by that limit. Sessions beyond the listing are still addressable by ful

l id or unique
prefix (core identity resolution is exhaustive and not capped by the listing limit).

The
command lists candidates and ambiguity hints from the bounded listing + watch set, then confirms

any prefix with the core resolver before a watch mutation.
- **No Git repository creation / clone /

general worktree management:** use shell tools, then
register the Workspace. The optional per-Sessi

on isolation described above only borrows an
already-composed experimental DSH worktree service; the

plugin itself performs no Git
operations — it does not create repositories, clone, fetch, merge, or

manage branches. The lead
must arrange review and merge/cherry-pick of an isolated branch (by dispa

tching it to a Session
or leaving it to the human), and existing Sessions cannot be re-homed into a

worktree.
- **Worktree isolation is best-effort and capability-gated:** without the experimental wor

Worktree isolation is best-effort and capability-gated:** without the experimental worktree
